sections.heading: Overview
bullets: Priya Raman led Q4 planning for Kestrel Dispatch around three bets: driver mobile app v2, an ETA-accuracy model, and a guided setup pilot for self-serve onboarding.
The team used Q3 churn of 4.1 percent, ETA accuracy of 82 percent within ten minutes, and a 19-day average onboarding time to judge priorities.

sections.heading: Key points
bullets: Amara Nwosu said support spends about 11 staff hours per new account cleaning the first import, while Daniel Ortiz said slow setup weakens sales momentum.
Jonas Weber framed mobile v2 around a clear stop list, a visible offline completion queue, and a completion control to be tested with drivers.
Lucas Ferreira proposed an 88 percent ETA accuracy gate and no worsening of misses over 40 minutes in meaningful cohorts, with weekend evidence and a rollback test.
Mei Tanaka estimated 30 effective engineering weeks for Q4 after leave, support, and maintenance.

sections.heading: Decisions
bullets: Priya Raman and Mei Tanaka agreed that mobile reliability takes priority and that guided setup pauses if it threatens the app's critical path.
Omar Haddad approved two backend searches and a capped four-engineering-week first stage for the onboarding pilot, while later compute and marketing spend depend on evidence.
The team allocated 14 engineering weeks to mobile, six to model evaluation and readiness, four to onboarding's first stage, and six to reliability reserve.
Hannah Cole will treat October as a pilot invitation window rather than announce general availability for all three bets.

sections.heading: Open questions
bullets: Jonas Weber and Mei Tanaka will choose between swipe-to-complete and explicit confirmation after observing at least eight drivers across three carriers.
Lucas Ferreira still needs to show whether the ETA candidate improves weekend freight lanes and stays inside Omar Haddad's compute ceiling.
The guided setup pilot must show whether five to eight selected accounts can reduce elapsed onboarding time and support effort without unsafe imports.

sections.heading: Pain points
bullets: Daniel Ortiz said buyers question a 19-day average wait to get their first live load and ask to see the driver workflow before buying.
Amara Nwosu said customers lose trust when offline driver actions are unclear or ETAs drift by more than 40 minutes.

sections.heading: Current solution
bullets: Kestrel Dispatch currently offers a driver app and ETA view, but Jonas Weber said drivers cannot always tell whether an offline completion reached dispatch.
New customers currently send files for assisted import, and Amara Nwosu said support spends about 11 hours per account on the first cleanup and mapping.

sections.heading: Budget and timeline
bullets: Omar Haddad approved two backend searches within existing compensation bands and capped onboarding's first stage at four engineering weeks.
Hannah Cole will prepare October pilot invitations, while public app promotion waits for the mobile reliability and customer readiness gates.

sections.heading: Objections
bullets: Mei Tanaka argued that a full self-serve launch would split scarce backend capacity across mobile sync, model serving, and import validation.
Hannah Cole objected to broad claims such as offline and self-serve until the supported actions and human review step are explicit.

sections.heading: Next steps
bullets: Daniel Ortiz will give sales a one-page roadmap by next week that distinguishes pilots from releases and uses the agreed gates.
Amara Nwosu will identify suitable pilot accounts and coordinate with Daniel Ortiz on customers whose ETA misses or onboarding delays affect renewals or evaluations.

sections.heading: Today
bullets: Priya Raman will post the Q4 decision log today and run a weekly review of the three bets.
Mei Tanaka will prepare the mobile release checklist and protect the six-week reliability reserve.
Lucas Ferreira will write the ETA evaluation plan and define the cohort dashboard.
Jonas Weber will prepare a completion-control prototype and a narrow onboarding flow.
Amara Nwosu will recruit driver testers and shortlist guided setup pilot accounts.
Hannah Cole will draft pilot invitations, customer FAQ content, and sales language.

sections.heading: Blockers
bullets: Mei Tanaka said the Android 14 crash regression and backend capacity could delay an app pilot or the guided setup stage.
Lucas Ferreira said GPU quota and weak weekend-lane evidence could block model promotion.
Jonas Weber said the dispatch board handoff still needs engineering review before its design decision is final.

sections.heading: Goals
bullets: Priya Raman set Q4 goals around a reliable driver app, ETA accuracy rising from 82 to at least 88 percent within ten minutes, and shorter onboarding than the current 19-day average.

sections.heading: Progress
bullets: Lucas Ferreira has a candidate ETA model that cut holdout mean absolute error from 11.8 to 9.6 minutes, though weekend-lane improvement is weaker.
Jonas Weber has defined the mobile jobs as a clear stop list, completion confidence, and recovery after losing signal.

sections.heading: Risks
bullets: Mei Tanaka identified offline sync conflicts, the Android 14 crash regression, and limited platform capacity as release risks.
Lucas Ferreira warned that an 88 percent blended ETA result could hide worsening misses on longer freight lanes.
Omar Haddad said unmeasured model compute and premature paid launch spending must stay behind stage gates.

sections.heading: Decisions
bullets: The team allocated 14 engineering weeks to mobile, six to model work, four to guided setup's first stage, and six to reliability reserve.
The team kept guided setup as a capped pilot that pauses before taking capacity from mobile reliability, resolving Mei Tanaka's objection to a full self-serve launch.
Public promotion requires Mei Tanaka's reliability sign-off and Priya Raman's approval of scope and evidence.

sections.heading: Next steps
bullets: Mei Tanaka will share the mobile checklist by Friday, and Lucas Ferreira will share the ETA evaluation plan by Friday.
Jonas Weber, Amara Nwosu, Hannah Cole, Daniel Ortiz, and Omar Haddad have separate prototype, pilot recruitment, message, roadmap, and hiring work due by next week.
